intro_html: Moroccan tagine sounds fancy, but it's really just chicken, chickpeas, and warm spices doing their thing all day. This bowl brings 62 grams of protein for about $4.74 a serving (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings means the cheapest ingredients feed you the longest.
cost_closing_html: About $4.74 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each serving lands at 62 grams of protein and 567 calories, hearty eating for barely over two dollars.
upsell_html: Cheap, cozy, and packed with protein. This is what a good slow cooker night looks like. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Canned chickpeas and tomatoes are pantry gold, so keep a few cans stocked and you can build this almost anytime.
Carrots and onions store for weeks, so buy them in bulk bags and let the cheap vegetables do the stretching.
Warm spices like cumin, cinnamon, and paprika are cheap in the bulk bin, so buy small scoops of each instead of full jars.
make_it: Add the chicken, drained chickpeas, diced tomatoes, chopped onion, sliced carrots, olive oil, broth, garlic, and lime juice to the slow cooker.
Stir everything together so the spices and liquid coat the chicken and vegetables.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the chicken shreds and the carrots are tender.
Shred the chicken into the stew and let it simmer together for a few minutes.
Spoon the tagine over white rice with plenty of the tomatoey broth.
